messages:
Elena (CEO): quick open-floor: thanks everyone for coming. want to use this thread for follow-ups on mission/positioning/roadmap. fire away and i'll answer as i can.
Sam (Head of Product): first q — when we say 'serving > owning models' how prescriptive are we? is this a sales pitch or an engineering stance?
Elena (CEO): both. productively it's our commercial differentiator: customers choose based on predictable latency/cost/SLA. technically it's our thesis for investing in runtime, routing, cache, and ops.
Maya (VP Eng): small tech follow-up: which runtime features are non-negotiable for the next 12 months? KV cache persistence? quantization profiles?
Priya (Research): we'll keep KV caching, continuous batching, and a 4-bit/8-bit quantization matrix top priorities. sequencing: cache + batching first (biggest perf wins), then quantization automation.
Ravi (Head of Sales): from GTM — how do we position vs hyperscalers who offer managed endpoints? customers ask about cost and lock-in.
Elena (CEO): short answer: hyperscalers sell infra; we sell predictable inference economics + developer UX across hosted/dedicated/private. emphasize: 1) unified API across environments; 2) cost controls (Optimize); 3) fallbacks to keep apps live.
Alex (Growth): any crisp one-liner for marketing? engineers want detail, buyers want something short.
Elena (CEO): try: "Run production LLMs with predictable latency, cost, and controls — anywhere you deploy." feedback welcome.
Kai (PM): roadmap question: when's the private/VPC GA and what limits will it have day 1?
Sam (Head of Product): planning GA in Q3 — initially regional private control plane, KMS integration, and audit logs. no on-prem air-gapped day 1; that's Q4.
Maya (VP Eng): also expect reduced throughput on initial private builds vs hosted as we validate autoscaling in customer environments. we'll publish perf profiles.
Ravi (Head of Sales): for enterprise conversations, what SLAs can we commit to on Dedicated today?
Elena (CEO): for Dedicated we can commit to uptime and latency SLOs in contracts (example: 99.9% uptime, p95 latency targets per model family). details vary by pool size and commit. Ask solutions for exact language.
Priya (Research): competitively, signal we support model adaptation for customers (fine-tuning / adapters) but we avoid owning model IP — we help them serve their models reliably.
Alex (Growth): pricing signal — will Optimize be bundled or add-on?
Sam (Head of Product): Optimize will be a tiered add-on initially (opt-in), then some heuristics will be default for free customers (safe batching thresholds).
Kai (PM): how do we measure 'positioning traction' — what metrics should teams watch?
Elena (CEO): good one — 3 metrics: 1) time-to-first-successful-prod-call (developer onboarding), 2) cost-per-1k-tokens for typical workloads (Cost delta vs naive infra), 3) % of customers using >1 deployment mode (hosted->dedicated/private).
Maya (VP Eng): small ops note: we'll add a dashboard row for those metrics in Console -> Adoption by Q2.
Ravi (Head of Sales): can we get a one-pager for enterprise on reliability guarantees + migration path from hosted->dedicated? helps close deals.
Sam (Head of Product): yes — putting that in the sales kit this week.
Elena (CEO): last note — if anyone wants deeper dives, i'm hosting office hours Fri 10am PT. i'll bring a roadmap sketch and competitive map. thanks all. :raised_hands:
all-hands-bot: thread pinned to #all-hands and answers recorded for follow-up.
